Marathon Petroleum fell 3% today after jumping nearly $12 over the previous two trading days, giving back some of those gains. The decline follows news that Russian crude production has rebounded sharply—the IEA reported output at 8.73 million barrels a day in October—which is pushing global oil markets back toward surplus (more supply than demand). This matters for refiners like Marathon because when global oil supply outpaces demand, crude prices typically soften, squeezing refining margins.

The broader context here involves a shift in market sentiment around oil supply. After weeks of tighter conditions, the return of Russian crude to the market signals that the supply-demand balance has swung, which can pressure both crude prices and the profit refiners make on each gallon processed. Meanwhile, heating oil prices remain elevated (up 59% year-over-year), which supports some demand, but the concern about rising shipping costs and cautious holiday retail inventory strategies suggests demand growth may slow heading into winter.
